title: Microsoft Teams Rooms: proximity join for attendees of Teams events
summary: Hold: the Bluetooth control's Learn link does not document the setting at the end of the printed path. The path and XML element are documented elsewhere in the cited sources, and the rollout, default and licensing statements are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated page for attendee proximity join in Teams events at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms attendee proximity join events town halls webinars licensing default admin switch; opened /microsoftteams/rooms/proximity-join and /microsoftteams/meetings-events-feature-comparison; results describe general proximity join or general event support.

claims.claim: General proximity join lets a user in the desktop or mobile Teams app invite or nudge a Teams Room into a meeting.
claims.quote: Proximity Join is a feature that lets end users use the Teams app on a desktop or mobile device to invite or nudge a Microsoft Teams Room into a Teams meeting.

claims.claim: Bluetooth beaconing is used to discover nearby Teams Rooms for proximity join.
claims.quote: Rooms discovered through Bluetooth are sorted by signal strength in descending order, and it includes all Teams Rooms both in use and not in use.

claims.claim: Ultrasound proximity signaling is available from compatible Teams Rooms on Windows consoles.
claims.quote: Ultrasound signaling is available on Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows (from compatible consoles) and can be used to along with Bluetooth for more accurate proximity join logic.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that every general proximity-join detail, including tenant and lobby rules, applies unchanged to events.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms proximity join events town hall webinar external anonymous lobby trusted tenant; opened /microsoftteams/rooms/proximity-join; read search excerpts from /microsoftteams/who-can-bypass-meeting-lobby and /microsoftteams/plan-events; no event proximity-specific rules stated.

claims.claim: The general Proximity Join page requires Bluetooth enabled on the room device and desktop or mobile client for proximity to function.
claims.quote: Bluetooth must be enabled on both the Teams Rooms device and on the client desktop/mobile endpoint in order for proximity to function.

claims.claim: All proximity-join communication takes place through Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: all communication takes place through Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Proximity join does not require a direct network connection between the user's personal device and the room device.
claims.quote: Proximity join doesn't require a direct network connection between a user personal devices and the Teams Rooms device

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described extra attendee or room data sent specifically by attendee proximity join in events.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms attendee proximity join events room attendee information data roster automatic join; opened /microsoftteams/rooms/proximity-join; read /microsoftteams/rooms/rooms-release-note roster-grouping excerpt; no event-specific extra data description found.

claims.claim: Bluetooth-discovered rooms are listed by descending signal strength.
claims.quote: Rooms discovered through Bluetooth are sorted by signal strength in descending order

claims.claim: Bluetooth discovery includes rooms both in use and not in use.
claims.quote: it includes all Teams Rooms both in use and not in use. This is because the Bluetooth signal isn't paused when Microsoft Teams Room has joined a meeting.

claims.claim: Bluetooth signals can pass through walls.
claims.quote: However, this signal can penetrate through walls.

claims.claim: General proximity-join nudges require a user from the same tenant or a trusted external organisation.
claims.quote: Proximity Join nudges from a desktop or mobile client must come from a user within the same tenant or from a trusted external organization.

claims.claim: General proximity join fails when the participant cannot bypass the Teams meeting lobby.
claims.quote: if the meeting participant using proximity join from their device is unable to bypass the Teams Meeting lobby, the proximity join will fail

claims.claim: Bluetooth use on Teams Rooms on Android is limited to advertising beacons and prompted proximal connections.
claims.quote: Bluetooth technology use on Teams Rooms on Android devices is currently limited to advertising beacons and prompted proximal connections.

claims.claim: Android proximity join involves no Bluetooth device pairing.
claims.quote:
Proximity Join, Better Together, Teams Cast, and pairing of Teams panels rely on Bluetooth.
There's no Bluetooth device pairing as part of these features.

claims.claim: No AI action or room joining an event on its own is described for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms attendee proximity join events room attendee information data roster automatic join; opened /microsoftteams/rooms/proximity-join and read MC1461157; sources describe user nudges and automatic acceptance, not AI or independently initiated event joins.

claims.claim: The attendee uses proximity join to bring a nearby room into the event.
claims.quote: Users will be able to use proximity join to connect to nearby Microsoft Teams Rooms when joining Teams events.

claims.quote: People or animals with sensitive hearing may be able to hear the ultrasound tones.

claims.claim: Rooms/ Phones > device > Settings > Device > Allow Bluetooth beaconing is documented by the row's pro-portal-settings link.
claims.quote:
Use the left navigation in the device panels to browse settings categories (About, Account, Meetings, Device, Network, etc.).
Modify the desired settings using the form fields.
claims.fix: Keep the printed path, which is supported by the portal navigation page together with the Device table. Set controls[0].ui.docs and its rendered Learn link to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/rooms/device-settings-available?tabs=WindowsSettings: that page documents Device > Allow Bluetooth beaconing. The current link gives generic navigation but neither names nor documents this setting.

claims.claim: SkypeSettings.xml exposes the BluetoothAdvertisementEnabled element for Bluetooth beaconing configuration.
claims.quote:
<BluetoothAdvertisementEnabled>true</BluetoothAdvertisementEnabled>
| `<BluetoothAdvertisementEnabled>` | Boolean ❷ | First ❶ | Enabled by default. |

claims.claim: Allow Bluetooth beaconing is a Windows Device-category toggle enabled by default.
claims.quote:
Teams Rooms on Windows
### Device
| Allow Bluetooth beaconing | Toggle | Enabled by default. | When checked, proximity-based meeting invitations using Bluetooth are automatically accepted.

claims.claim: The Pro Management portal exposes an Ultrasound beaconing setting for Windows devices.
claims.quote: Under Device, turn on Ultrasound beaconing and, if needed, Automatically accept proximity-based meeting invitations.

claims.claim: Windows ultrasound configuration includes Automatically accept proximity-based meeting invitations.
claims.quote: When selected, supported proximity-based meeting invitations are automatically accepted. This setting appears when Ultrasound beaconing is enabled.

claims.claim: Configuring device settings in the Pro Management portal requires Rooms Management role-based access control permissions.
claims.quote: you can configure settings for Microsoft Teams devices (Teams Rooms on Windows, Teams Rooms on Android, Teams Panels and Teams Phones), provided you have the necessary role-based access control permissions for Rooms Management.

claims.claim: The SkypeSettings.xml configuration route applies to Teams Rooms on Windows.
claims.quote: At startup, if a Microsoft Teams Rooms console finds an XML file named SkypeSettings.xml located at `C:\Users\Skype\AppData\Local\Packages\Microsoft.SkypeRoomSystem_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState`, it applies the configuration settings

claims.claim: Learn recommends the portal's individual and bulk configuration options instead of XML.
claims.quote: We recommend using the individual and bulk settings configuration options within the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal instead of the XML configuration.

claims.claim: Microsoft says it no longer publishes new XML settings.
claims.quote: We no longer publish new XML settings but all settings are managable within the Portal.
